question: During the Gupta period, 'Bhagvatism', which emphasized bhakti and ahimsa, centered on the worship of which deity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vishnu**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Bhagvatism** emerged during the **Gupta period**, emphasizing **bhakti** (devotion) and **ahimsa** (non-violence), which were central tenets of Hindu philosophy. 
• It was primarily centered on the worship of **Lord Vishnu**, who was considered the preserver in the Hindu trinity of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. 
• During the Gupta period, **Vaishnavism** (worship of Vishnu) gained prominence and became one of the dominant religious practices. 
• Bhagvatism promoted the idea of a personal relationship with God through devotion and love, marking a shift from ritualistic practices to emotional and spiritual connection. 
• The Gupta rulers, such as **Chandragupta II**, were great patrons of Vaishnavism, and many temples dedicated to Vishnu were built during this era. 
• Texts like the **Bhagavad Gita** and **Puranas**, especially the Vishnu Purana, played a significant role in spreading the teachings of Bhagvatism and strengthening its philosophical base. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Lord Vishnu:** 
• He is known as the **preserver** in the Hindu trinity and is associated with qualities such as compassion, protection, and sustenance. 
• Vishnu is often depicted as resting on the cosmic serpent **Shesha**, with his consort **Lakshmi**, the goddess of wealth, by his side. 
• His ten incarnations, known as the **Dashavatara**, include famous forms like **Rama**, **Krishna**, and **Narasimha**. 
• Vishnu Purana and Bhagavad Gita serve as key texts elaborating on his role and teachings, emphasizing dharma and devotion. 
• **The Gupta Empire:** 
• The Gupta period (320-550 CE) is known as the **Golden Age** of India for its advancements in art, literature, science, and religion. 
• The rulers were patrons of Hinduism, especially Vaishnavism, and contributed to temple architecture and iconography. 
• Key temples dedicated to Vishnu include the **Dashavatara Temple** at Deogarh and other structures showcasing intricate carvings and depictions of Vishnu’s avatars. 
• **Bhakti Movement:** 
• Bhagvatism laid the foundation for the later **Bhakti Movement**, which spread across India during medieval times. 
• It emphasized devotion over rituals, promoting a personal connection with God. 
• Saints like **Meerabai**, **Kabir**, and **Chaitanya Mahaprabhu** carried forward the ideals of bhakti, making religion accessible to all social classes. 
• **Other Deities in Hinduism:** 
• **Shiva:** Known as the destroyer, worshipped in Shaivism, he symbolizes transformation and renewal. 
• **Brahma:** The creator in the Hindu trinity, though his worship declined significantly over time. 
• **Indra:** A Vedic deity associated with rain and thunder, primarily worshipped during earlier Vedic times but less prominent during the Gupta era. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Bhagavad Gita:** 
• It is part of the **Mahabharata**, a sacred text advocating devotion, dharma, and selfless action. 
• The Gita serves as a philosophical guide for understanding the principles of Bhagvatism. 
• **Vaishnavism’s Influence:** 
• Many Gupta coins featured images of Vishnu and his avatars, showcasing the empire's allegiance to Vaishnavism. 
• The religious practices of the time were inclusive, with a focus on unity and spiritual growth. 
• **Ahimsa:** 
• This principle of non-violence was integral to Bhagvatism and influenced subsequent religious movements like Jainism and Buddhism.
